comparisons.peer_topic: Stock-based compensation valuation models and expense recognition policy
comparisons.peer_summary: The Company uses the Black-Scholes and Monte Carlo simulation models to estimate the fair value of stock options, RSUs, and ESPP shares at the grant date. Compensation expense is generally recognized using the straight-line method over the vesting period, with forfeitures estimated at grant and revised if necessary.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and AMD disclose their methodologies for valuing stock-based compensation and recognizing expense for similar award types (RSUs, market-based PSUs, and ESPP). Both companies use the closing trading price (minus dividend discount) for standard RSUs and Black-Scholes for ESPP. NVIDIA uses Monte Carlo simulation for market-based PSUs, while AMD uses it for RSUs with market conditions; both apply straight-line expense recognition for these standard awards. A key difference is the recognition method for performance-based awards: NVIDIA uses an accelerated amortization model for corporate-target PSUs, whereas AMD recognizes expense for RSUs with performance or market conditions (PRSUs) ratably for each vesting tranche from the service inception date, rather than a generic accelerated model described in the summary.

sentences.text: We use the closing trading price of our common stock on the date of grant, minus a dividend yield discount, as the fair value of awards of restricted stock units, or RSUs, and performance stock units that are based on our corporate financial performance targets, or PSUs.
We use a Monte Carlo simulation on the date of grant to estimate the fair value of performance stock units that are based on market conditions, or market-based PSUs.

The compensation expense for RSUs and market-based PSUs is recognized using a straight-line attribution method over the requisite employee service period while compensation expense for PSUs is recognized using an accelerated amortization model.

We estimate the fair value of shares to be issued under our employee stock purchase plan, or ESPP, using the Black-Scholes model at the commencement of an offering period in March and September of each year.
Stock-based compensation for our ESPP is expensed using an accelerated amortization model.
The Company estimates stock-based compensation cost for stock options at the grant date based on the option's fair value as calculated by the Black-Scholes model.
For time-based restricted stock units (RSUs), fair value is based on the closing price of the Company's common stock on the grant date.
The Company estimates the grant-date fair value of RSUs that involve a market condition using the Monte Carlo simulation model.
The Company estimates the grant-date fair value of stock to be issued under the Company's Employee Stock Purchase plan (ESPP) using the Black-Scholes model.

Compensation expense is recognized over the vesting period of the applicable award using the straight-line method, except for the compensation expense related to RSUs with performance or market conditions (PRSUs), which are recognized ratably for each vesting tranche from the service inception date to the end of the requisite service period.
